fields.sections.0.h: Nationwide Flight Operations Suspended for Over 5 Hours
fields.sections.1.h: Communication and Radar Instability Due to Router Overload
fields.sections.2.h: Over 3,500 Aircraft in Flight and Large-Scale Passenger Impact
fields.sections.3.h: Cyber Attack Ruled Out, Medical Flights Continue Operating
fields.sections.4.h: Issue with Legacy Analog Equipment, Not New AI System
fields.sections.5.h: Congressional Budget Approval Shortfall and Infrastructure Modernization Delays
fields.sections.6.h: Control Tower Confusion and Pilot Response
fields.sections.0.ko: On Friday, November 13, 2026, at 3:54 p.m., the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration issued an order halting departures at all airports nationwide. Authorities did not disclose specific reasons but announced only 'special circumstances and safety considerations,' and with approximately 7,000 flights canceled, airports across the nation filled with stranded passengers. This measure lasted over 5 hours before being lifted at 8:15 p.m.
fields.sections.1.ko: Transport Secretary Sean Duffy explained at a White House press conference that a router in the legacy air traffic control system experienced data overload, causing instability in radar and communication systems nationwide. Authorities emphasized that they decided on the precautionary measure of suspending operations after discrepancies appeared in radar data and communications with aircraft became irregular. The stance is that while there was no complete loss of communication and radar capability overall, the decision was made for safety reasons due to the instability.
fields.sections.2.ko: At the time of the flight suspension, there were over 3,500 aircraft over U.S. airspace, and according to real-time flight tracking service Flightradar24, 4,042 flights bound for U.S. destinations were in the air. According to estimates by aviation logistics experts, approximately 300,000 to 400,000 passengers are expected to have been stranded. As time passed, Reagan Washington National Airport and Chicago O'Hare Airport reached parking capacity, requiring aircraft to be diverted to other airports.
fields.sections.3.ko: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullin stated there were no signs of a cyber attack and there was no danger to public safety. While authorities do not have complete certainty, the current evidence suggests this was not a malicious attack. Meanwhile, medical flights such as organ transplants were permitted to continue operating during the suspension period.
fields.sections.4.ko: Secretary Duffy attributed the root cause of this incident to the air traffic control system using decades-old legacy analog equipment, and noted that disruptions from the same issue have continued in recent years. For example, there was an incident in May 2025 when the radar screen at Newark Liberty International Airport went out for 90 seconds. Air Space Intelligence, the developer of the FAA's new artificial intelligence-based air traffic control system SMART System, clearly stated that their software was not responsible, and Duffy confirmed that the system was completely separate from the problematic equipment.
fields.sections.5.ko: Secretary Duffy urged Congress to approve $50 billion for infrastructure modernization, stating that the legacy equipment will continue to fail. Congress approved $12.5 billion last year for air traffic control upgrades over five years, but the Secretary's request is far larger in scale, suggesting that the pace of improvements has been insufficient. The Secretary stated that he expects U.S. airspace to return to normal before the Thanksgiving travel season arrives.
fields.sections.6.ko: Controllers at Newark Airport's control tower described the situation as 'complete chaos' in real-time voice feeds and mentioned space constraints and gate issues. Some controllers said they were not receiving information from higher authorities. An aviation safety expert explained that pilots have received training for communication failure situations, and with a multi-layered communication system by altitude, safe aircraft separation can be maintained through alternative means even in the event of altitude control center failures.
fields.sections.7.ko: A passenger on a flight from Indianapolis to Chicago testified that he initially heard it was a radio issue but later received notification that the situation was more serious. While he is a consultant assisting with AI technology adoption, he noted this was his first experience of such an incident, and said passengers showed mixed emotional reactions. After the flight suspension was lifted, major airlines including Delta, United, and American began resuming operations.
fields.sections.8.ko: A nationwide flight suspension is extremely rare in U.S. aviation history. It occurred once in 2001 following the 9/11 attacks and once in January 2023. In January 2023, flight operations were suspended for several hours due to a pilot warning system malfunction, which was caused by contractor personnel accidentally deleting a file during a database synchronization process. This 2026 incident will be recorded as the second major event occurring after a gap of over 10 years.
fields.caveat: Since the article was written in November 2026, it addresses future events from the current reader's perspective, and based on immediate statements from government officials, the technical root cause analysis may change in the future.
